comments.author: spectramax
comments.story_title: Turbo, an Improved Rainbow Colormap for Visualization
comments.why_zh: 说明了导致 Viridis 诞生的 Jet 缺点
comments.quote_zh: 这些缺点正是创建 Viridis 的原因，这场精彩的演讲对此做了例证
comments.text_zh: > 今天我们很高兴介绍 Turbo，这是一种新的色图，具有 Jet 的理想特性，同时也解决了它的一些缺点，例如虚假细节、条带和色盲歧义。Jet 的理想特性是什么？为什么不使用 Viridis 或 Magma，或 matplotlib 2.0 中任何近期线性色图？这些缺点正是创建 Viridis 的原因，这场精彩的演讲对此做了例证：[VIDEO] 我不理解 Turbo 的意义。 > Turbo 模仿 Jet 的明度分布，从低到高再回到低，且没有条带。因此，它的明度斜率通常是 Viridis 的两倍，使细微变化更容易被看到。这是一个有价值的特性，因为当颜色可用于区分低端和高端时，它能大大增强细节。为什么会有人想要低-高-低色图？ > Viridis 是一种线性色图，通常在需要伪彩色时被推荐，因为它对眼睛友好，并且解决了 Jet 的大多数问题。Inferno 具有与 Viridis 相同的线性特性，但对比度更高，因此更适合挑出细节。然而，有些人觉得它可能刺眼。虽然这不是出版时关心的问题，但当人们必须长时间检查可视化时，它确实会影响人们的选择。个人品味 vs 科学准确性——我会选择后者，除非我们是在为营销材料做图。在我看来，这不是有根据的理由
comments.text: > Today we are happy to introduce Turbo, a new colormap that has the desirable properties of Jet while also addressing some of its shortcomings, such as false detail, banding and color blindness ambiguity. What are the desirable properties of Jet? Why not use Viridis or Magma or any of the recent linear colormaps from matplotlib 2.0? These shortcomings were the exact reason why Viridis was created as exemplified in this brilliant talk: [VIDEO] I don't understand the point of Turbo. > Turbo mimics the lightness profile of Jet, going from low to high back down to low, without banding. As such, its lightness slope is generally double that of Viridis, allowing subtle changes to be more easily seen. This is a valuable feature, since it greatly enhances detail when color can be used to disambiguate the low and high ends. Why would anyone want low-to-high-to-low colormap? > Viridis is a linear color map that is generally recommended when false color is needed because it is pleasant to the eye and it fixes most issues with Jet. Inferno has the same linear properties of Viridis, but is higher contrast, making it better for picking out detail. However, some feel that it can be harsh on the eyes. While this isn’t a concern for publishing, it does affect people’s choice when they must spend extended periods examining visualizations. Personal taste vs scientific accuracy - I will take the latter unless we are doing plots for marketing materials. In my view this is not substantiated reason

comments.text_zh: 我构建了类似的感知均匀颜色库：[LINK] 令人遗憾的是，我们在物理世界中拥有所有这些颜色，但在 sRGB（甚至 Adobe RGB 或 DCI P3）空间中表示会剥夺所有乐趣。我们可用的空间很窄，这限制了你所能做的事情。世界上绝大多数显示器几乎无法表示 sRGB 空间，即使能表示，校准又是另一个问题。你可以运用各种科学来正确表示颜色，但如果最终用户的校准不好，一切就都无法保证。颜色是界面设计（以及无障碍）的一个问题；在处理定量数据并构建兼顾无障碍考虑的感知均匀色图时，它就成了真正的挑战。这里有一场关于 Matplotlib 新色图的精彩演讲：[VIDEO]
comments.text: I built similar perceptually uniform color library: [LINK] The sad part is that we have all these colors available in the physical world but representing in sRGB (or even Adobe RGB or DCI P3) space takes away all the fun. We have a narrow space to work within and it poses limits to what you can do. Vast majority of monitors in the world are barely capable of representing sRGB space, and even if they are, calibration is another issue. You can employ all kinds of science in representing proper colors but if the end user's calibration is not good, all bets are off. Colors are a problem for interface design (and accessibility), it becomes a real challenge when dealing with quantitative data and build perceptually uniform colormaps with accessibility considerations, here is an amazing presentation of Matplotlib's new colormaps: [VIDEO]

comments.author: CorrectHorseBat
comments.story_title: Rainbow Color Map Still Considered Harmful (2007) [pdf]
comments.text_zh: 你是在以强烈的局部失真为代价来提高可区分性，我看不出这怎么会是一个好的权衡。做个对比，你更愿意要哪个：一张不失真的图，还是一张平均大约大三倍、但严重失真的图？它在有些地方比原图小，在另一些地方又大五倍。你真的会选择那张更大的图吗？jet 就是这样。看看这张图 [VIDEO]（有时间的话把整个视频看完），理想情况下你会希望导数（左上角那两张图）保持恒定，这样才不会扭曲你的数据。jet 到处乱跑，而 viridis 基本恒定（幻灯片里没展示，但导数一直保持在 120 左右）。
comments.text: You're increasing the discriminability at the cost of high _local_ distortion, I don't see how that is a good tradeoff. As a comparison, what would you rather have: a non-distorted plot or a plot that is on average about three times as big, but it's heavily distorted. At some places it's smaller than the original and on other places it's 5 times bigger. Would you really choose the bigger figure? That is what jet is. Look at this plot [VIDEO] (watch the whole video if you have the time), ideally you want the derivatives (the 2 plots on the left top) to be constant so not to distort your data. Jet is all over the place while viridis is basically constant (not shown in the slides, but the derivative stays all the way around 120).

It's colourful, so those without colour blindness get a richer display than if you used greyscale, and the colours chosen aren't too affected by most common forms of colour blindness. But for those that really can't see the colours, even if you literally just convert to monochrome, it still works. comments.text: That's a... surprisingly good question. I'm actually a physicist by background first, so I got my start doing waaayyy too many calculations with blackbody and emissions spectra. Then, back in 2010, when I was just getting into startups, I spent two weeks straight at Powell's in Portland reading through their graphic design section. After that, I never got very far away from light or perception... AR/VR -> graphics -> silicon photonics -> physical AI (now). I'm still very much learning, but if you like this stuff and want to learn more yourself there's a couple sources I can recommend: - Interaction of Color, by Josef Albers. Amazing book, but you really want to get a physical copy. - I really like this talk from SciPy 2015 to get a sense of how people work with and talk about color maps in practice: [VIDEO] - This is a really, really thorough (and beautifully illustrated) article on what color spaces are: [LINK] - And last, I wrote a very technical blog post a few years back, if you want to see some math on a bunch of this: [LINK]

comments.text_zh: 你的评论让我想起那些关于 Matplotlib 信息展示问题的演讲[0][1]。我觉得很多设计是在没有意识到无障碍问题的情况下做出来的，而这更广泛地说是文化问题，而不是技术问题。这种情况可以通过技术手段（操作系统或硬件层面的感知）改善，也可以通过我们集体教育设计应该考虑哪些问题来改善。通常，当设计考虑到无障碍时，设计会变得更好，但当设计师或开发者没听说过这些问题、也没有处理它们的工具时，无障碍往往被视为障碍。有好的工具在这里很有帮助。情况似乎正在改善，但需要时间。我上小学时，大字本教科书得特别订购，有声书是有的，但需要特殊的磁带和播放器。可以用便携式 CCTV 来放大很小的字。所有这些设备都很专门、昂贵，而且对大多数人来说很难获得。所有这些都已被我手机内置的功能取代了。特别要提一下 iOS 上的“Zoom”应用，它有针对色彩敏感问题人群的颜色滤镜，也有针对小字的增强文本渲染（不幸的是，它有 bug，有时会崩溃），但这比为了让一些数字放大而让相机胶卷里塞满菜单或路由器底部的随机照片要好得多。[0] [VIDEO] [1] [LINK]
comments.text: Your comment reminded me of the talks on the issue of information display for Matplotlib[0][1]. I think a lot of design is done without awareness of accessibility and this is more broadly a cultural thing than a technical thing. The situation can be improved both by technical means (OS or hardware awareness) as well as by our collective education about what kinds of issues designs should consider. Typically, designs become better when they account for accessibility, but it is oftentimes seen as a hurdle when a designer or developer has not heard about the issues and also is not equipped with tools to handle them. Having good tools is helpful here. The situation seems to be improving, but it will take time. When I was in elementary school, you had to special order large print text books, audio books were available, but required special tapes & players. A portable CCTV could be used to magnify small print. All of this equipment was specialized, expensive and hard to come by for most people. All of this has been replaced by features built into my phone. Special shoutouts to the "Zoom" app on iOS, that thing has color filters for people with color sensitivity issues and enhanced text rendering for small print (unfortunately, it's buggy and crashes sometimes), but it is much better than littering my camera roll with random pictures of menus or the bottom of routers just so I can zoom in on some numbers. [0] [VIDEO] [1] [LINK]

comments.text_zh: > 我不明白你的意思，线性（dL'star'）是相对于感知均匀性定义的，CIELAB 76 按定义（近似地）不也是线性的吗？？而且颜色算术按定义几乎就意味着在感知均匀颜色空间中处理距离和角度，不是吗？？不。线性是关于物理光强与感知颜色的关系。想象同一位置有两个光源，你可以分别打开或关闭它们。如果打开第一个，你会感知到某种颜色；如果打开另一个，你会感知到另一种颜色；如果两个都打开，你会感知到第三种颜色。事实证明，（在正常观看条件下）可感知的颜色（对大多数人来说）可以表示在三维向量空间中，使得对于任意两个可能的光源，前两种颜色相加得到第三种颜色。例如 XYZ 就是这样的线性颜色空间 [1]。这与感知均匀性无关。感知均匀性是关于区分相近颜色的能力。它定义了颜色之间的距离，而有些三维颜色空间表示能让欧几里得距离很好地近似这种感知距离。cieLAB 就是这样的颜色空间，但据我所知，出于同样的目的还有更好的最先进颜色空间。我不太精通这个，我是从这个视频 [2] 学到的。[1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO] 编辑：gimp 2.10 现在默认使用线性颜色空间（不是感知均匀的！）fo
comments.text: > I don't get what you mean, linearity (dL'star') being defined wrt perceptual uniformity, isn't CIELAB 76 linear by definition (to an approximation) ?? And color arithmetic pretty much by definition implies dealing with distances and angles in a perceptually uniform color space, doesn't it ?? No. Linearity is about physical light intensities relating to perceived color. Imagine having two light sources on the same spot that you can turn on or off separately. If you turn the first one on you perceive a certain color, if you turn the other on you perceive an other color and if you turn both on you perceive a third one. It turns out the perceivable colors (under normal viewing conditions) are representable in a three dimensional vector-space (for most people) so that the first two colors add up to the third color for every possible two light sources. Such a linear colorspace is XYZ for example [1]. This has nothing to do with perceptual uniformity. Perceptual uniformity is about the capability of distinguishing near colors. This defines a distance between colors, and there are three dimensional colorspace representations where the Euclidean distance approximate this perceptual distance well. cieLAB is such a colorspace, but AFAIK there are better state of the art colorspaces for the same purpose. I'm not very well versed in this, I learned from them from this video [2]. [1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO] edit: gimp 2.10 now defaults to use a linear colorspace (not perceptually uniform!) fo
